clues: This city stands on the north bank of a great river in South Texas. Just across the water lies a town in Mexico, its twin.
High hills to the west block damp air from the far Pacific side. That dry shield helps make summers fierce and rain quite scarce here.
Set up in 1755, this town grew from a small village on the river. For a short time it ruled as the head town of its own republic.
Each year this city throws a huge long party for the first US leader's birth day. The fest runs for weeks and draws huge crowds of guests.
Four bridges for road traffic and two rail bridges cross the wide river here. They link this port town to the land just south.
